extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and stakeholders who use FederalRegister.gov (commenters, document drafters, researchers, and developers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for locating Federal Register documents, preparing and submitting comments, and using FederalRegister.gov features and developer resources. Includes procedural limits (what the site can and cannot do), drafting resources, accessibility and linking practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission channel limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Our “Site Feedback” tool and Federal Register email addresses are only intended for users to submit technical questions and comments on the functionality of the FederalRegister.gov website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools cannot be used to submit comments on rulemaking actions or to petition agencies on public policy issues. The Office of the Federal Register (OFR) has no authority or ability to process comments on rulemaking actions—do not use site feedback/email to attempt to file regulatory comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: New 'Submit a Formal Comment' feature (integration with Regulations.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to comment on a document without leaving FederalRegister.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This feature was developed in collaboration with Regulations.gov; use it to submit formal comments through the integrated workflow rather than site feedback. (Implicit guidance: follow the formal comment workflow presented on a document's page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and use of the Public Inspection page
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Inspection web page on FederalRegister.gov offers a preview of documents scheduled to appear in the next day's Federal Register issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Public Inspection page may also include documents scheduled for later issues (at the agency's request). Use it to access important or complex documents before they publish in the daily Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document features — active links in document text
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency has included links as part of the document text, we activate those links using the text in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links may not work if the link in the published document contained an error or if the target website is no longer at that location. (Be cautious relying on embedded links; treat them as preserved from the agency's text.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Document utility bar and sidebar features
rubrics_metrics.description: The utility bar runs along the left side of the document and scrolls with you down the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can access the Public Inspection version and the official electronic format of the published document using the two bottom icons. Use the printer icon to print, and use sharing icons (email, social) as provided. (Guidance: use these UI controls to access alternate formats and share/save documents.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Document Drafting & Research resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Links to materials that help understand the document drafting process and research Federal Register documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources include: Drafting Document Drafting Handbook; Incorporation by Reference (IBR) Handbook; Federal Register Bulletins; Final Guidance on Implementing the Plain Writing Act of 2010 (PDF); Federal Register Plain Language Tools; PlainLanguage.gov; Thesaurus of Indexing Terms; GPO Page. Use these authoritative guides when preparing documents or submissions to ensure conformity with FR drafting practices and citation/indexing standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use plain language and Plain Writing Act guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Guidance on Implementing the Plain Writing Act of 2010 and Federal Register Plain Language Tools are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting Federal Register documents or comments, apply plain-language principles and available tools/resources to improve clarity and accessibility of text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking and citation conventions for FederalRegister.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register documents can be cited in a variety of ways; it may be convenient to link to FR documents in different patterns depending on the document and your preferred pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site provides explained patterns and examples for linking and citation. Follow the provided patterns when referencing FR material so links and citations are consistent and navigable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search tips and techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: This site has a basic search tool and an advanced search. The basic search box appears in the main navigation at the top every page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'Search' pull-down for options: Document Search (search by citation such as '75 FR 12345' or '75 Fed. Reg. 12345'), Public Inspection Search, and advanced filters. Apply appropriate search fields and citation formats to locate documents efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saving documents for later (MyFR clippings)
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov allows users to save documents for later use via a MyFR feature named 'clippings'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents can be clipped from the document’s page or from search results. Click the flag icon to add the document to your clipboard. Use MyFR account features (clippings, subscriptions, clipboard) to manage documents you intend to review or comment on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developer resources, REST API, and data access
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register data originates with files used to produce print and PDF editions and are transformed into bulk XML files made available by the GPO. Additional MODS metadata files are also produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the site’s REST API and interactive documentation to access bulk data; the FederalRegister.gov team maintains a Ruby API client gem. The site is open source with repositories (federalregister-api-core and others) available on GitHub—use these resources for automated retrieval, linking patterns, or building tools that consume FR data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility compliance and assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The site is designed following Section 508 and W3C accessibility design guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site uses text-based files and PDFs that are text-accessible through Adobe PDF tools. For access assistance or accessibility concerns, refer to the Accessibility page and contact provided accessibility contacts. (Guidance: follow Section 508/W3C practices and available instructions for visually impaired users.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and legal status of Federal Register publications
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov is an authorized service of OFR (NARA) and the GPO and is committed to protecting the privacy and security of visits to the website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site follows OMB recommendations and best practices for Internet privacy. Also: Federal Register publications, the site, CFR indexes, and Public Laws posted on FDsys.gov are not subject to FOIA requests—understand this legal status when seeking records or submitting inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and support channels — editorial vs technical
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact channels differ by purpose: fedreg.info@nara.gov for editorial content/questions, and a support ticket system for programming/technical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate contact method depending on the issue: editorial/content questions vs site programming/technical problems. For questions on access for the visually impaired, use the Accessibility contact. Do not use these contacts to file regulatory comments.
